articles.title: MLB playoff power rankings 2026: From the Astros to the Dodgers, which teams are ready to go on a World Series run?
articles.summary: We've had 162 games to assess these 12 teams. Here's how they stack up as the October tournament begins.
articles.body:
It took until Game 162 to finalize the field , but we've made it through the marathon and arrived at the real prize that is MLB's postseason . While 18 teams started their offseasons on Sunday, the dozen qualified clubs shifted into a new gear with another month of high-stakes baseball in front of them.

To some degree, the start of the postseason represents a reset. But each team's case as a World Series contender is mostly rooted in their performance in the regular season, both over the entirety of the past six months and more recently as October approached. Better records earn more favorable paths to the Fall Classic in the form of first-round byes and home-field advantage. Then again, many superior seeds have faltered in recent years, offering reminders to expect the unexpected in October.

All that said, we've had 162 games to assess the quality of each club before the October tournament begins. The chase for a championship starts now. Here's how the 12 teams left stack up.

Jump to a team by clicking on the links below:

Houston's eight-year postseason streak was snapped last year, when it won 87 games and were left out on account of losing a tiebreaker to Detroit . This season, the Astros went .500 — their worst record in a full season since 2014 — but still won the AL West and are headed back to the postseason.

It required a disastrous Mariners campaign and painfully mediocre Rangers club to enable this division title, but the Astros will take it, and they deserve credit for finding a way into the dance on the final day of the season . Their roster is notably more shallow than every other postseason club's — especially on the mound — but Houston boasts a handful of impact individuals who could sway the series in its favor.

MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez leads the way as a downright horrifying hitter for opposing pitchers to deal with, and the Astros also have a pair of terrific infield bats in Isaac Paredes and Jeremy Peña , who could ease the offensive burden. On the mound, a ton is riding on Hunter Brown to be at his best every time out, and if the Astros can cobble together enough innings otherwise (far from a guarantee) closer Josh Hader looms large on the backend. While much lighter than the loaded rosters the Astros carried over the past decade, this Houston club has just enough star talent to be reasonably competitive.

Is there a modicum of disappointment in the White Sox's final postseason seeding, having spent the majority of the second half atop the AL Central? Certainly. But for this team, qualifying for the postseason after losing 324 games the previous three seasons (yes, that's a real number) is astounding enough on its own and a whale of a triumph for the organization in every sense. The mounting (and unexpected) pressure to finish the job as division champs might have caught up to Chicago somewhat in the final weeks — it's little surprise that a seasoned contender in Cleveland took advantage — but now that the Sox have arrived in the postseason, they should be able to return to their longstanding mindset of "playing with house money," which has seemingly fueled this young roster all year.

And this group didn't get here by accident. There's talent worth taking seriously, even if only a handful of players on the roster ( Andrew Benintendi , Randal Grichuk , Tommy Pham ) have any postseason experience. The White Sox were the only team in the majors with three 30-plus-homer hitters ( Munetaka Murakami , Miguel Vargas , Colson Montgomery ), a nice trio to bring to the postseason party, where changing the game with one swing is often paramount. The rest of the lineup features a variety of less slug-happy skill sets, with contact mavens such as Chase Meidroth and standout rookies Tristan Peters and Sam Antonacci. The rotation is notably thin, but if the offense is humming — and if the underrated bullpen can shorten games to manager Will Venable 's liking — there's enough here for the White Sox to extend their storybook season.

A comfortable cushion earned with a scorching midsummer stretch — the Red Sox went 32-5 (!!!) from June 25 to Aug. 7 — meant Boston didn't have to sweat much to secure a wild-card spot. But it's difficult to ignore how poorly the Red Sox performed down the stretch, particularly at the plate, where Boston ranked as one of the league's weakest offenses in September by most metrics . Add the unfortunate sequence involving Game 162 against the Cubs being moved to Tropicana Field to avoid weather in Boston, only to have that final game be meaningless given how the NL wild-card field shook out , and the Red Sox are entering the postseason with some uneasy vibes.

But considering how poorly the first half of this season went, Boston has to be feeling good about having reached this point, and now another clash with the rival Yankees awaits in Bronx — a rematch of last year's wild-card showdown, with a healthy amount of fresh faces. Chief among them is new skipper Chad Tracy. Rising superstar Roman Anthony was injured for the postseason last year but seemed to be heating up in recent weeks, even as the rest of the offense floundered. Willson Contreras has been one of the best hitters in the American League this season; we'll see if his hand injury compromises his impact.

And even without a fully available Garrett Crochet , the Red Sox are quite stout on the mound, with a rock-solid veteran righty in Sonny Gray , a rookie southpaw standout in Payton Tolle and a proven postseason performer in lefty Ranger Suárez . The bullpen is terrific beyond that trio, so getting outs should not be Boston's tallest task in October. Whether the scuffling lineup can score enough, however, remains to be seen.

The Phillies stared into the abyss on the final day of the season and said, "We're not done yet." A cathartic victory over the Rays punched the team's ticket to the postseason after a miserable final week threatened their participation altogether. Now the Phillies head to Atlanta to take on their division rivals , marking their first meeting in the best-of-three first round after they faced off in the NLDS in 2022 and 2023. It is both a terribly tough task — the Braves thoroughly outclassed the Phillies in the regular season, and the Phillies won't have their ideal rotation, having needed ace Zack Wheeler for Game 162 — and a golden opportunity for Philadelphia to flush its ugly form over the final few weeks and restore its status as one of the NL heavyweights.

The top of this roster still stacks up well with almost any other across the league, with Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper serving as offensive anchors with excellent postseason résumés. Wheeler's availability in this wild-card series is yet to be determined, but it was good to see lefty Jesus Luzardo on the mound in Sunday's game after he missed most of September due to a shoulder issue. Recall that Luzardo's last outing before his trip to the injured list was a 12-strikeout shutout against the Braves; his availability in the upcoming series could be enormously consequential.

If Philly's third ace, Cristopher Sánchez, can provide enough quality innings to limit the limited bullpen's exposure, Jhoan Duran awaits in the final frames as one of the league's best closers. Bats beyond Schwarber and Harper will need to wake up for Philadelphia to make a deep run, but there are just enough championship-caliber ingredients in place that it would be foolish to discard this team too quickly.

Rallying from six games back on Aug. 16 was a piece of cake compared to the historic September surge Cleveland delivered to claim the division crown a year ago. And here the Guardians are in the postseason once again — AL Central champs for the seventh time in the past 11 seasons — with another quality shot at ending the league's longest championship drought. Not only do the Guardians have a favorable path, thanks to a first-round bye secured in this year's underwhelming American League, but also there are elements of this Cleveland club that inspire more confidence than recent iterations .

The offense ranks as the weakest in the field statistically, just like it did a year ago, but the personnel has changed enough to suggest a more potent attack is possible. A pair of rookies in Chase DeLauter and Travis Bazzana have been a big boost, and trade-deadline acquisitions Jo Adell and Nathaniel Lowe have provided the kind of power and veteran presence that prior Cleveland lineups lacked. Even in a down year, José Ramírez is one of the toughest outs in the league, with pesky leadoff man Steven Kwan not far behind.

The Guardians will also enter the division series with a rested pitching staff led by standout rookie lefty Parker Messick and strikeout machine Gavin Williams , a dynamic duo followed in the later frames by a quality bullpen headlined by shutdown closer Cade Smith . At various points along the way, the Guardians have barely resembled a contender, floundering through stretches of uninspiring baseball. But when everything is clicking, they look awfully dangerous. We'll see which version shows up in October.

With the best offense in the majors by most measures, the Cubs will have to mash their way to the World Series, given the plethora of questions on the mound. A broadly similar sentiment followed Chicago last year, but there's a strong case to be made that this year's offense is more dangerous. That obviously starts with the mega-breakout of Pete Crow-Armstrong , who was batting seventh (!) for the Cubs last postseason and has since blossomed into one of the best players on the planet and an all-around wrecking ball atop the lineup. Chicago also swapped Kyle Tucker for Alex Bregman — arguably an upgrade in any context, but especially come October, considering Bregman's spectacular track record in the postseason.

Even if hitters such as Michael Busch , Nico Hoerner and Dansby Swanson haven't produced nearly as gaudy statlines as last year, they're quality hitters capable of supporting the superstars atop the batting order. So no matter how you slice it, this lineup should be a handful for opposing pitchers, and that should give Chicago a fighting chance in every game. Massive questions remain regarding how manager Craig Counsell can patch together enough outs in the later innings, but if trade-deadline acquisitions Clay Holmes and Kevin Gausman can provide some stability and holdovers Matthew Boyd and Shota Imanaga can limit the longball, the Cubs could make a real run.

Aaron Judge 's availability ( or lack thereof due to his calf injury ) looms large, and that's to be expected when talking about a three-time MVP. But even without Judge, the Yankees go into this postseason with a ton of high-end talent on both sides of the ball, especially relative to the rest of the AL.

Cam Schlittler announced himself in the wild-card series a year ago, with 12 strikeouts across eight scoreless innings against Boston, and now he has a full season of ace behavior solidifying him as one of the best starting pitchers on any postseason club. That makes Max Fried , a metronome of run prevention, one of the best No. 2 starters around, and gives New York an enviable 1-2 punch to set the tone in any series, with veterans Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón serving as valuable rotation depth. The bullpen lacks the big names of years past, but it has quietly been quite effective; only the Red Sox (3.00) enter the postseason with a lower reliever ERA than the Yankees (3.15).

On offense, Ben Rice delivered the full-season breakout that many had been waiting for, and he and Cody Bellinger give New York a pair of upper-echelon lefty bats atop the lineup. Trade-deadline adds Luis Garcia Jr. and Heliot Ramos have been a mixed bag, but their contributions — as well as those of rookies Spencer Jones and George Lombard Jr. — will carry significant weight if Judge cannot participate. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is another star-level talent who has produced like a star only in spurts; now would be a great time for him to heat back up. A Judge-less Yankees offense will need to find a bit more juice somewhere — maybe even Giancarlo Stanton can produce a big swing or two — but the pitching might be good enough to make a deep run regardless.

Like the Astros, the Braves are back in the postseason after a rare miss last year, restoring a familiar look to the NL side of the bracket. A mess of a Mets season and an ice-cold start from the Phillies meant Atlanta sat in first place uninterrupted from mid-April to the end of the regular season, with their lead atop the NL East swelling as high as 10.5 games and never falling below three after July. Now the Braves will welcome the rival Phillies to town for the wild-card series , with ace Chris Sale 's long-awaited postseason debut as a Brave looming in Game 1.

That Sale continues to splash around in the fountain of youth and remains one of the best pitchers in the league is a huge deal for the Braves, especially considering their dearth of impact rotation arms beyond him. Right-hander Tyler Mahle 's run prevention since arriving at the deadline has been outstanding (1.99 ERA across 54 ⅓ innings), but can that be replicated in his postseason debut at age 31? Atlanta's shallow rotation should be helped at least in part by its tremendous bullpen, which recently got reinforced further by the return of Robert Suárez .

But in general, this team will go as far as its stars take it, from Ronald Acuña Jr. to ironman Matt Olson to breakout backstop Drake Baldwin to the mercurial Michael Harris II . Rarely have all these hitters been hot at the same time, but if they catch fire simultaneously over the next month, a serious postseason run could be in store.

For the first time in franchise history, the Padres have reached the postseason for a third consecutive year. They rode a red-hot September to not only a wild-card spot but also the right to host the Cubs in the first round at what should be a raucous Petco Park. This is quite the development considering how dire things got: A series loss on July 23 in Atlanta dropped San Diego to 50-53, with its playoff odds plummeting below 10% , per FanGraphs. But from that point forward , the Padres went 41-18 — the best record in baseball over that span — and surged to another postseason berth behind a reinvigorated offense and a dominant bullpen.

Since hitting his first home run of the season on May 30 (!), Fernando Tatis Jr. has been playing at an MVP level. Jackson Merrill has been fantastic in the second half, and Ty France — a minor-league signing in February — has been the unsung hero of this offense (141 wRC+), enjoying a career year with the franchise that drafted him in 2015. While deadline adds Robbie Ray and Casey Mize have been mostly disappointing, Nick Pivetta returned from injury just in time to strengthen the top of the rotation alongside Michael King .

And it's no secret that this team is in strong position to shorten ballgames. A wealth of high-leverage relievers are available for rookie manager Craig Stammen , from the lefties Yuki Matsui , Wandy Peralta and Adrian Morejon to the traditional flamethrowers such as Bradgley Rodriguez to the ultimate game-ender in Mason Miller . It's a picturesque postseason bullpen, so if San Diego can produce leads for that unit to protect, this team is going to be difficult to deal with.

In a season defined by historic levels of mediocrity in the American League, the Rays floated above the fray en route to the third-highest win total in franchise history. Their dominance was perhaps best exemplified by their proclivity to sweep opponents: Tampa Bay logged 16 undefeated series in the regular season, by far the most of any team (the Dodgers were second with 13, Red Sox third with 11). They were especially excellent at Tropicana Field — 55-26 marks the second-best home record in a full season in franchise history, behind that of the pennant-winning 2008 club (57-24) — delivering an impressive showing after spending last season away from home due to the damage from Hurricane Milton. With home-field advantage secured through the AL side of the bracket, the Rays' success in St. Petersburg could spell exciting things for the month ahead.

Leading the charge is the electric Junior Caminero , a force of nature in the batter's box with the personality and clutch factor to carry a team to great heights. His co-stars in the lineup are the steady Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda , but don't sleep on role players such as rookie Victor Mesa Jr. and speedy Chandler Simpson , who have emerged as key contributors. And deadline acquisition Liam Hicks has been exactly the upgrade behind the dish that Tampa Bay had been seeking. This isn't the highest-powered offense in the postseason, but the Rays' bats are more than enough in tandem with their stellar pitching staff anchored by a true frontline arm Drew Rasmussen and supported by an army of funky arm angles, sizzling stuff and ultra-deep arsenals. This is a complete ballclub that stands out even more in this year's American League.

Is this finally the year? The Brewers are in the postseason for the eighth time in the past nine seasons, but all Milwaukee has to show for that is a pair of NLCS exits at the hands of the Dodgers. That this small-market franchise has repeatedly defied projections to rack up a boatload of regular-season wins has been unquestionably impressive, but at some point, the regular-season success needs to be an appetizer, rather than the main course. Just like last year, the Brewers enter the postseason with the best record in the majors and a new franchise record for wins , but their small-ball recipe has many around the industry doubtful that such an outfit can thrive against the other top dogs in October.

Why might this year be different? It starts on the mound with Jacob Misiorowski , who was an ascendant rookie flamethrower last year; now he's a super-ace who might be the best pitcher on the planet. Logan Henderson 's stuff doesn't wow like the Miz's, but only five starters (Misiorowski, Sale, Tarik Skubal , Schlittler and Williams) have a higher strikeout-minus-walk rate than the 24-year-old rookie. Brice Turang , Jackson Chourio and Jake Bauers have each elevated their games from good to great, giving the lineup a higher ceiling. The bullpen is elite once again, with both left- and right-handed weapons at manager Pat Murphy's disposal.

The rotation beyond Misiorowski and Henderson is shaky at best, and the relative lack of over-the-fence pop (28th in home runs) are ominous red flags, but overall, this team looks like a supercharged version of last year's club. We'll see if that's good enough to topple the Dodgers or whoever else gets in the Brewers' way en route to their first Fall Classic since 1982 — and perhaps their first World Series title ever.

The Dodgers have looked much more vulnerable this season, as their collective age has shown up in both injuries and inconsistency on offense. But this behemoth still wields two enviable traits in spectacular starting pitching and an unmatched wealth of postseason experience, and that earns L.A.'s offense the benefit of the doubt, despite the cold stretches that surfaced throughout the summer. This collection of outrageously accomplished hitters didn't always produce at juggernaut levels in the regular season, but with such an abundance of talented bats, L.A. needs only a few of them to catch fire to provide the requisite run support for this exceptional pitching staff.

Shohei Ohtani 's impact atop the lineup, having navigated a few injuries in recent weeks, is an obvious X-factor, but there's comfort in knowing that Mookie Betts played his best ball in September, and Kyle Tucker, who also appeared rejuvenated down the stretch, adds a new wrinkle to the lineup. Pairing Tarik Skubal with a proven October titan in Yoshinobu Yamamoto atop the rotation was exactly the kind of maneuver that reflects the Dodgers' relentless pursuit of another championship, and Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow give L.A. arguably the best No. 3 and No. 4 starters of any postseason team. This massive edge in the rotation helps make up for a bullpen that has thinned out due to injuries but still features several quality arms.

Are the Dodgers unbeatable? Not even close. We saw how narrow the margins were last October, and this year's National League field could present some daunting matchups. But based on what this group has overcome thus far — and the talent they've added to improve their chances — the Dodgers are the favorites until proven otherwise. Let's see if they can deliver on the hype.

articles.title: Cleveland Guardians Cut 26-Year-Old For 6-Foot-6 Hurler Before MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians cut one 26-year-old player just to add a 6-foot-6 pitcher before the MLB playoffs. The post Cleveland Guardians Cut 26-Year-Old For 6...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians are off to the MLB playoffs. They ended their regular season with a 2-3 loss to the Kansas City Royals . With another Guardians playoffs series on the horizon, news has emerged regarding Craig Yoho .

The Guardians finished first in the AL Central Division with an 85-77 record. The Chicago White Sox finished second, the Minnesota Twins finished third, while the Detroit Tigers and the Royals finished fourth and fifth, respectively.

Cleveland Guardians Cut 26-Year-Old For 6-Foot-6 Pitcher Before Facing The Chicago White Sox Or Houston Astros

Before their final game of the 2026 season, the Guardians announced a couple of transactions. One of those transactions involved Yoho.

According to the MLB Transactions Log, the Guardians optioned Yoho while recalling another pitcher: "Cleveland Guardians optioned RHP Craig Yoho to Columbus Clippers. Cleveland Guardians recalled RHP Austin Peterson from Columbus Clippers."

Yoho is a 26-year-old pitcher who was acquired from the Milwaukee Brewers at the MLB Trade Deadline. Austin Peterson is a promising 27-year-old pitcher who stands 6-foot-6 and weighs 234 pounds.

Yoho and Peterson have had two very different 2026 seasons.

Yoho has split his season between the Guardians and Brewers. Before being traded, he recorded 18 strikeouts in 20 innings, to go along with a 3.15 ERA, one hold, and a 0.85 WHIP in 15 games pitched.

After the trade, he played 19 games. In those games, Yoho collected 23 strikeouts, one blown save, and three holds, with a 6.87 ERA and a 1.64 WHIP in 18.1 innings.

As for Peterson, he played only two games for the Guardians and spent most of his season in the minors.

Peterson spent the entire season in Triple-A, starting 21 games and making 23 appearances. He finished with 107 strikeouts, a 5-9 record, a 4.41 ERA, and a 1.41 WHIP.

No matter which player is up with the Guardians, the team reached this point because of the collective efforts of everyone in the organization. If they make it to the World Series, it will also be because of the collective efforts of everyone on the team.

articles.title: Yankees' Aaron Judge Provides Injury Update, Talks Status for Red Sox Series in 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: New York Yankees fans are anxiously waiting to see whether Aaron Judge will be available for the start of the playoffs on Tuesday, but the slugger didn't have an answer on Monday.
articles.body:
New York Yankees fans are anxiously waiting to see whether Aaron Judge will be available for the start of the playoffs on Tuesday, but the slugger didn't have an answer on Monday.

"I think a lot of things. I don't make those decisions," Judge told reporters. "We'll see how today goes and we'll have a better answer for you at the end of this."

Judge added that he's "feeling great" ahead of the series against the Boston Red Sox.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone was likewise uncertain of Judge's status for Game 1 against the Red Sox.

"I don't know. We'll continue to evaluate and I'll listen to trainers and medical and see where we're at," Boone told reporters.

Judge missed the majority of the regular season because of a rib injury, but was able to return earlier this month. His return lasted just seven games, as he suffered a right calf strain and landed on the injured list to end the regular season.

While Judge said that he's feeling good, he added that he has not yet run the bases, a major step in returning from a lower-body injury.

Boone implied last week that Judge would not be available for the wild-card series against the Red Sox, saying that the Yankees are "planning on him not being a part of that" and adding that Judge has a "moderate" calf strain.

Judge didn't seem to agree with that notion, though.

"I don't know why he used those words," Judge told reporters .

In the seven games following his return, Judge hit just .174/.208/.304 with one homer and 13 strikeouts in 24 plate appearances. While he's still clearly shaking off some rust, the Yankees would be in a much better position to beat the Red Sox if he's able to play.

Whether New York will have its star in Game 1 on Tuesday remains to be seen.

articles.title: Aaron Judge wants to play in the wild-card round — will the Yankees include him on the roster?
articles.summary: Judge took live batting practice during the Yankees' workout on Monday.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Aaron Judge would like to play baseball. That much is clear.

Whether the New York Yankees include their leading man on the upcoming wild-card roster is a much hazier situation.

Judge has not seen game action since Sept. 16, sidelined due to a right calf strain. Before that ailment emerged, Judge missed three months due to a stress fracture in his rib. He returned on Sept. 8, went a lackluster 4-for-23, hurt the calf and went right back on the shelf. As such, his status for New York's best-of-three playoff showdown with the Boston Red Sox has been a story of great intrigue across the tri-state area.

On Monday, beneath a glum, pewter sky, Judge and the Yankees went through the typical pre-postseason series workout. The three-time MVP took four or five rounds of light batting practice on the field. He uncharacteristically flared a ball foul into the seats. He also clobbered one over the wall in deep left-center. To an amateur's eye, he looked like a physically compromised version of Aaron Judge, though it's impossible to make a complete diagnosis from 30 swings against a soft-tossing coach.

About a half-hour later, Judge stepped in for a live at-bat against an up-down reserve hurler named Elmer Rodríguez. Teammates and team officials filed into the home dugout to watch. Rap music bounced from the stadium speakers. Skipper Aaron Boone perched in his usual spot, arms slung over the railing. Media members gathered in the seats behind home plate. The yard bubbled with anticipation as the Yankees' most important character dug his spikes into the box.

Then Judge saw five pitches and swung at none of them, drawing himself a "walk" back to the dugout. He returned minutes later for another plate appearance, this time against southpaw Ryan Weathers . Judge drew another free pass, though not before swinging through a down-and-in breaking ball. His third at-bat finished with a well-struck bounder that ricochetted off Rodríguez's glove. His fourth at-bat was, again, swingless.

Little learned, little gained. Judge's status, as of Monday evening, is unchanged. Nobody will know anything for certain until full rosters are released Tuesday morning.

"I'm feeling great," Judge told reporters before the workout. "Been doing a lot of work back there to try to get back as soon as I can. Been swinging it for a couple days. Moving around. Excited to get on the field today to see what we can do."

"He's making progress," Boone said earlier in the day. "We'll continue to see where he's at."

While it seems incredibly unlikely that Judge, who, as of Monday morning, had yet to run the bases, would be capable of playing right field on Tuesday, both player and manager refused to rule out the possibility. Still, given Judge's reduced state, it's difficult to envision him galloping around the Yankee Stadium outfield. If he plays against Boston, expect it to be as a DH or pinch hitter.

Even that possibility raises its own set of questions. Between Ben Rice , Paul Goldschmidt and Luis García Jr., the Yankees' roster is overflowing with first base/DH types. The potential return of Giancarlo Stanton , out since April due to calf issues of his own, would further cloud that picture. Stanton also took live at-bats Monday, one of which ended with a vintage Stantonian laser to shortstop.

Considering how both goliaths looked and Stanton's long history of slugging through various maladies, Stanton seems like a more viable pinch-hit option at this point. Carrying Judge on the roster over a defensively useful character such as Amed Rosario might be foolish if Judge is a diminished version of himself. There's also the potential for a more significant injury; Judge's calf muscle could theoretically give way and put his Achilles at risk. Giving the future Hall of Famer a few more days of rest and hoping the rest of the roster can eke past the Red Sox might yield the Yankees' best chance of getting the slugger back closer to full strength later in October.

Judge, surely, would disagree with that assessment. His approach thus far has been both delusional and admirable, featuring hubris and grit, teetering between irresponsibility and resilience. It's difficult to envision the Yankees playing a postseason game without him . He certainly can't. That's part of why, at every turn, Judge has remained publicly adamant that he'll be physically able to participate in the wild-card round.

But what Judge wants is secondary to what the Yankees decide is best. The captain's self-confident, grit-it-out-at-all-costs schtick matters only if Boone, GM Brian Cashman, the medical staff and the other pinstriped powers-that-be buy into it.

Judge is willing. Able is a different thing entirely.

articles.title: Dan Wilson announces his own firing as Seattle Mariners manager in rare postgame moment
articles.summary: Dan Wilson broke MLB protocol by personally announcing his own dismissal as Seattle Mariners manager, delivering an emotional postgame address.
articles.body: Seattle Mariners manager Dan Wilson personally broke the news to his team and the media Sunday that he will not return for the 2027 season. Before Game 162 against the Los Angeles Angels, Wilson held a closed-door meeting to inform players and staff. Postgame, he stepped to the podium to deliver the news publicly and face questions before front-office executives addressed reporters. Standard MLB protocol calls for front-office executives to issue a news release or hold a solo news conference while the ousted manager stays out of sight. A manager taking the microphone to announce his own dismissal is virtually unheard of in modern sports. "This season has been very difficult, and of course, the results have not been what any of us have expected," Wilson said. "As a result, it's concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners." Wilson, a former Mariners catcher who took over as manager in August 2024, acknowledged his deep roots in the organization. "I'm still processing this with my family, and it's a very difficult day," Wilson said. "We love this city. We love this community and we appreciate the organization for what it has meant to the family since coming here as a player in '94. We feel extremely blessed by all the opportunities we've been afforded." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Expectations were sky-high entering 2026. Coming off a 2025 AL West title and reaching Game 7 of the ALCS, Seattle fell just one win short of the World Series. Instead, the club collapsed to a 76-86 third-place finish. The downward spiral was driven by offensive regression among core players, inconsistent starting pitching, a second-half bullpen collapse and some of the worst defensive metrics in Major League Baseball. Late-season comments from players highlighted a lack of clubhouse accountability as a core failure. Pressed on whether leadership failed to enforce standards, Wilson faced the criticism directly. "That's always a necessary component, and I think accountability comes in a lot of different ways," Wilson said. "Obviously, I think you look back, and there's a lot of things that you can point to, and perhaps that's one of them." When asked if the front office made the final decision, Wilson accepted the reality of sports leadership. "I've been in baseball a while, and this is what happens," Wilson said. "Managers shoulder the blame and shoulder the responsibility. And this is obviously difficult." RED SOX REMOVE INTERIM TAG FROM MANAGER CHAD TRACY AFTER THE TEAM'S REMARKABLE SUMMER TURNAROUND Seattle Mariners President of Baseball Operations Jerry Dipoto and General Manager Justin Hollander will return in 2027. Dipoto noted that "collectively we failed to meet our own expectations" and agreed a leadership change was necessary. Wilson finishes his tenure as Mariners manager with a 187-171 career record. New York Mets president David Stearns acknowledged on Monday that the decision to let star first baseman Pete Alonso depart in free agency—and the moves made at the position to replace him—didn't work out so well.

The 31-year-old Alonso had another fantastic season, hitting .267 with 43 homers, 113 RBI and a .884 OPS.

The Mets, meanwhile, got 18 homers, 77 RBI and a .667 OPS from the players they utilized at first base this season, primarily Jared Young and Mark Vientos. Meanwhile the splashy offseason additions like Bo Bichette, Luis Robert Jr., Jorge Polanco, Marcus Semien and Freddy Peralta all disappointed.

Hindsight is 50-50, as Stearns well knows. But letting a beloved, multi-time All-Star walk in free agency is normally a bad decision.

articles.title: How former NFL, MLB greats helped develop Lakeland football's Cam Fuse
articles.summary: Here is how Lakeland's Cam Fuse uses family, former NFL and MLB greats to bolster the Lakeland football and baseball programs.
articles.body:
Gallery: Lakeland, Tenoroc in action in Week 5

Lakeland junior wide receiver Cam Fuse ran a quick hitch route before hauling in a pass from quarterback Kelin Hendrix and scampering in for a 32-yard touchdown. It ultimately helped the Dreadnaughts secure a 49-14 win over Auburndale Friday at home.

"I loved this game with the guys. We got to showcase our talent out there on the field. We practiced really hard. And that practice really showcased on the field," Fuse said.

These practice habits stamped the No. 13 team in Florida at 4-1 on the year. Fuse was instrumental in helping Lakeland win big, as he racked up three catches for 54 yards and a score. But he doesn't rest on his laurels, and he augments his skill set from some of the very best that have ever played the game.

Fuse, a two-sport star who plays football and baseball, has family who played football and baseball at the highest level: former NFL receiver Anquan Boldin and Major League infielder Dee Strange-Gordon are his cousins. Boldin was a three-time Pro Bowler and Super Bowl champion with the Baltimore Ravens and Gordon was a two-time all-star, Gold Glover, Silver Slugger, batting champion and a three-time stolen bases leader.

And these aren't family members who Fuse sees now and then because of his busy schedule; rather, along with speaking with them regularly, he incorporates them into his training schedule to polish his skill set in both sports. Over this past summer Fuse and Boldin worked out together at a park, working on route running and footwork. And with Gordon, Fuse is able to take advantage of his batting cages while also training together.

Fuse said he fully intends to utilize his professional resources to accomplish team goals for the Lakeland football and baseball programs in 2026-27.

Specifically in football, Fuse started flag football when he was 7 in an Avon Park youth league.

As he navigated through the weights trying to find himself as a player, he studied the game of New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Fuse landed the former LSU great because of his dance moves, creativity to get open, his route running and his spectacular catches, especially the one-handed, 43-yard touchdown reception on Nov. 23, 2014, against the Dallas Cowboys .

With Beckham Jr.'s inspiration and Fuse constantly playing backyard football with his friends, the future pass catcher convinced his mom to eventually let him play football. Fuse would go on to play football, arduously training in sand to develop his speed while also training with Boldin, who helped him make a name for himself early on.

His family moved to Lakeland two years ago.

"It was really the opportunity at Lakeland (that made me want to play there). Me and mom had a talk eighth-grade summer and we decided on Lakeland," Fuse said.

A couple years into the Dreadnaught powerhouse, Fuse has already been a part of some teams that have made it all the way to state. And in those moments, he said that he has gleaned a lot of information, including life moments and football situations from head coach Marvin Frazier and assistant coach Henderson Taylor.

The 6'2, 180-pound receiver takes his coaching seriously and has developed himself into one of the best wide receivers in Polk County, as he runs his routes crisp and he attacks the ball at the highest point.

"I'm a humble kid. I just stick to the grind. I'm not a kid that will go party or anything like that," Fuse said.

Fuse through five games is up to 17 receptions for 328 yards ― with a season-long of 85 — and a score. More importantly, the Dreadnaughts have won four of five and are well on their way to accomplishing their goals.

"Cam's a leader. (He's) played a lot of football (and) has been a starter since his second game as a freshman. (He's) definitely a locker room guy that all of the kids enjoy and respect," Frazier said.

Fuse has his immediate goals for this season and for after 2028 when he graduates. But right now, big-time colleges have eyes on him including Minnesota , Auburn, Florida State, Kansas State, among other schools.

Lakeland (4-1) will next play the SFA Rams Friday at home.

articles.title: Ranking Every 2026 MLB Playoff Team's Starting Lineup
articles.summary: The 2026 MLB postseason begins on Tuesday. While a strong pitching staff remains arguably the most important factor in a deep playoff run, more than a few World Series hopefuls have been stopped in their tracks by an ice-cold offense.
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB postseason begins on Tuesday. While a strong pitching staff remains arguably the most important factor in a deep playoff run, more than a few World Series hopefuls have been stopped in their tracks by an ice-cold offense.

To that point, the Philadelphia Phillies (19th), Boston Red Sox (23rd) and Cleveland Guardians (24th) are the only teams in this year's playoff field that did not rank in the upper half of the league in runs scored. All three rank inside the top 10 in starting pitching ERA.

Ahead, we've taken a closer look at the projected lineup for each of the 12 playoff clubs and ranked them based on impact talent, injury questions, overall depth and recent performance.

1. SS Jeremy Peña 2. DH Yordan Alvarez 3. 3B Isaac Paredes 4. 2B Jose Altuve 5. C Yainer Diaz 6. 1B Christian Walker 7. CF Lucas Spence 8. RF Cam Smith 9. LF Taylor Trammell

Bench: C Christian Vázquez, IF Nick Allen, IF Raynel Delgado, OF/1B LaMonte Wade Jr., OF Nelson Velázquez

One-Sentence Outlook: The Astros have the presumptive AL MVP in Yordan Alvarez, but the rest of the offense has produced a .233/.300/.396 line this year. He will need to replicate his memorable performance in the 2023 ALCS for pretty much the entirety of October.

Injury Questions: Daulton Varsho, Jake Meyers and Brice Matthews all landed on the injured list in September. All three will be out of action for at least the wild card round, with Meyers done for the year.

Lineup Construction: Infielder Raynel Delgado has a solid chance of being the 14th position player on the roster for the Wild Card Series. He would provide some insurance for Isaac Paredes at third base after he fouled a ball off his knee on Saturday.

X-Factor: Lucas Spence went 6-for-18 with four home runs in five games after being recalled from Triple-A when Varsho and Matthews were placed on the injured list. He suddenly looks like the no-doubt starting center fielder for the club's playoff run.

1. CF Steven Kwan 2. 3B José Ramírez 3. RF Chase DeLauter 4. DH Jo Adell 5. 2B Travis Bazzana 6. 1B Nathaniel Lowe 7. LF Angel Martínez 8. C Patrick Bailey 9. SS Brayan Rocchio

Bench: C Austin Hedges, 1B/OF David Fry, IF Angel Genao, IF/OF Daniel Schneemann

One-Sentence Outlook: The Guardians ranked 26th in OPS (.696), 27th in home runs (162) and 24th in runs per game (4.19) during the regular season, once again leaning heavily on the pitching staff to punch their playoff ticket.

Injury Questions: The only position player currently on the Guardians' injured list is Rhys Hoskins. He has been sidelined since Aug. 18 with lower back inflammation, but he has been taking batting practice at the team's "stay ready" camp and could add some pop off the bench if he's available.

Lineup Construction: David Fry and Austin Hedges have both been seeing regular action against left-handed pitching. Both the catcher and first base positions will likely continue to be straight platoons in October.

X-Factor: José Ramírez hit just .229/.296/.302 after returning from a fractured left hamate bone in July, followed by an even worse .198/.237/.264 in September. It's hard to see Cleveland making it deep into the postseason without him heating up at the plate.

1. DH Kyle Schwarber 2. SS Trea Turner 3. RF Bryce Harper 4. 1B Alec Bohm 5. 2B Bryson Stott 6. LF Brandon Marsh 7. 3B Edmundo Sosa 8. C J.T. Realmuto 9. CF Justin Crawford

Bench: C Rafael Marchan, C Garrett Stubbs, IF Otto Kemp, OF Bryan De La Cruz, OF Derek Hill

One-Sentence Outlook: Veteran sluggers Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber were the only players on the Phillies' roster this season with at least 100 plate appearances and an OPS+ of 100 or better.

Injury Questions: Luis Arraez suffered an ankle sprain that sidelined him for the final three games of the season, and he will not be included on the Wild Card roster. Otto Kemp will be recalled from the minors to replace him on the roster, while Edmundo Sosa will almost certainly move into the starting lineup.

articles.title: Athletics' Zack Gelof suing Tigers after July knee injury at Comerica Park
articles.summary: Gelof suffered a deep laceration on his right knee and missed a month of action.
articles.body:
Athletics utility player Zack Gelof has filed a 16-page lawsuit against the Detroit Tigers, Ilitch Holdings and the Detroit-Wayne County Stadium Authority following an injury he suffered while playing at Comerica Park.

During the Athletics' 4-1 loss to the Tigers on July 9, Gelof left the game in the bottom of the third inning after making a sliding catch in left field foul territory. According to WDIV , the lawsuit alleges that the 26-year-old suffered a serious knee injury after he collided with exposed metal fencing along the side wall.

Gelof claims that he suffered a deep laceration below his right kneecap that was close to his patellar tendon. He left the game shortly after the catch and did not return to action until Aug. 10.

The lawsuit argues that the metal fencing was sharp and not protected enough and that the defendants should have understood the area could be a part of play.

Gelof's attorneys allege that weeks after his injury protective padding was added to the area in question.

"It doesn't take a stadium design expert to realize that sharp metal fencing in an area where players are required to slide and play around is a recipe for disaster like the one that occurred here," said attorney Jon Marko in a statement. "All they had to do was put cheap padding up like they did after Zack was injured, and this entire incident could have been avoided."

Comments made by Tigers outfielder Riley Greene are cited in the lawsuit, reflecting that players are aware of that area of the field.

"That portion of the fence where he hit is metal," Greene said after the July 9 game . "He kind of slid into it, and it's definitely going to hurt if you slide into it."

The complaint seeks to recover damages for lost wages, pain and suffering, as well as attorney fees and costs.

articles.title: MLB Free Agents 2026 Rumors, Predictions Before AL, NL Wild Card Games
articles.summary: The 2026 MLB playoffs have arrived.
articles.body:
Of course, that means for 18 of the league's less fortunate franchises, the offseason is here for them, too.

It'll be a tricky one to navigate due both to the expiring labor contract and the fact this pool of free agents runs pretty shallow. Beyond superstar starter Tarik Skubal, there may not be a can't-miss difference-maker to be found.

Still, the Skubal sweepstakes should be a fascinating watch, and there are plenty of talented pros up for grabs. Let's dissect the latest rumor-mill rumblings and predict what they might mean moving forward.

Brandon Lowe Set to Capitalize on Power Surge?

How's this for a quick temperature check on Lowe's sizzling market? One rival executive recently summed him up as such to FanSided's Robert Murray : "He's a f***ing beast, bro."

If timing is to MLB free agents what location is to realtors, then this two-year run from Lowe is his beachfront estate. Since the start of 2025, the slugging second baseman has tallied 66 homers, 179 RBI and 173 runs over 284 games.

Those are monstrous numbers—especially for a player at his position—and they are sure to drive up tons of interest on the open market. Speaking of which, Murray wrote that there are "plenty of teams eagerly awaiting the chance to sign" Lowe.

Between Lowe's proven pop and improved defense, he has a chance to strike it rich this offseason. He very well may have priced himself out of Pittsburgh.

Prediction: Lowe signs a three-year deal with the New York Yankees.

Big Payday Still Coming for Freddy Peralta?

There were myriad reasons that things went south for the New York Mets this season, but Peralta's massively disappointing tenure with the team felt bigger than most. He was brought in to serve as the ace of this staff and promptly buckled under that pressure, posting a 4.99 ERA and the worst strikeout rate of his career across 22 starts.

You might think, then, that this makes Peralta a prime candidate to sign a short-term, prove-it type of contract. And while that could be where things ultimately land, it sounds like teams are willing to bet bigger on both his pre-NY track record and post-NY recovery with the Tampa Bay Rays (3.25 ERA over 10 starts).

As one executive told FanSided's Robert Murray , Peralta "will do just fine" in free agency. Murray added that Peralta "is regarded as one of the best clubhouse guys in baseball."

If teams sense Peralta would be cheaper to sign now than he would've been, say, last offseason, that might embolden them to present him a longer contract pitch in hopes of locking him in at a potentially discounted rate. Saying that, it's probably in his best interest to take a shorter deal with a higher salary in hopes of performing on that pact and re-entering the market to eventually strike it richer than he can right now.

Prediction: Peralta signs a two-year deal with the San Diego Padres.

Massive Market Forming for Tarik Skubal?

There are two ways to view Skubal's prominent perch atop this free agent class. Some will feel as if they have to go get him, since there may not be any other needle-movers on the other board. Others could feel his isolation in the rankings will inflate his price to impossible heights.

It sounds like the typical deep-pocketed franchises will comprise that former group. Per FanSided's Robert Murray , "the expectation is that just about all of the big-market teams will be bidding on the superstar left-hander." Murray added that Skubal "should top the current record for a free-agent contract given to a starting pitcher, currently held by Yoshinobu Yamamoto at $325 million."

That price tag will surely price out a lot of teams, especially in this highly uncertain economic environment. If Skubal would settle for a shorter deal with higher annual salaries, maybe a few surprise clubs could place bids with bloated salary figures, but his market feels fairly predictable.

In short, the crystal ball sees this coming down to the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—two of the biggest spenders in baseball. The Dodgers just made an aggressive move for Skubal at this year's trade deadline, while the Mets badly need a boost to their rotation. This bidding war should be ferocious, but in the end, the Dodgers' head start by having Skubal already on the roster could be what pushes them over the edge.

Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers on a 10-year deal.

articles.title: Aaron Judge Injury Update, Latest Status as Yankees Announce Roster for Red Sox Series
articles.summary: After being placed on the injured list two weeks ago with a calf injury, New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge won't be ready to play in the team's American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
After being placed on the injured list two weeks ago with a calf injury, New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge won't be ready to play in the team's American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox.

The Yankees officially left Judge off of the team's roster for the matchup with the Red Sox. Jack Curry of YES first reported on Judge's status.

New York and Boston will start their series with Game 1 on Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium.

Judge missed the bulk of the 2026 regular season because of a fractured rib, and just seven games after returning to action from that injury, he landed back on the IL with a calf issue.

On Monday, Judge participated in batting practice for the first time since suffering the injury, and he told reporters that he was trying to make a push to be ready for the Wild Card Series.

"I've been doing a lot of convincing," Judge said. "I feel like I'm going to keep doing that. But I think the most important thing is just making sure I'm healthy and ready to go for this long stretch. We got another month of baseball to play so I want to be ready for the long run we're going to go on here for this next month. We're all going to be smart, but I think they all know I want to be out there, especially that first game."

Yankees manager Aaron Boone had previously told reporters that he did not expect to have Judge available for the Wild Card Series, but that didn't stop Judge trying to make a late push to be included on the roster.

After winning back-to-back AL MVP awards in 2024 and 2025, Judge was nowhere near his normal level of production this season.

Appearing in just 66 games, Judge slashed .241/.360/.511 with 18 home runs and 41 RBI.

Aside from the COVID-shortened season of 2020, those marked Judge's lowest homer and RBI totals since 2016, which saw him appear in only 27 games as a rookie.

Despite not having Judge for most of the season, the Yankees still managed to finish 93-68, giving them the second-best record in the AL.

However, since the Tampa Bay Rays won the AL East with a 98-64 mark, the Yankees have to take the more difficult road of going through the Wild Card Series in order to reach the American League Division Series.

Had the Yankees gotten a bye into the ALDS, it may have improved the chances of Judge not having to miss any playoff time.

As for ALWCS, the Yankees will be without their best player, but they still have plenty of offensive firepower from the likes of Ben Rice, Cody Bellinger and Co.

However, it is their pitching that makes them favored to knock off Boston with a starting rotation of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodón.

If the Yanks can get past the Red Sox in the ALWCS and make it to the ALDS against the Rays, it will give Judge a few more days to get ready and potentially still give him a chance to make an impact in the playoffs.

articles.body:
The MLB playoffs officially begin on Tuesday, and the rosters for the Wild Card round have been unveiled.

Teams had until 10 a.m. ET on Tuesday to submit their final rosters for the start of the postseason.

While multiple teams had to make tough roster decisions based on untimely injuries, the most glaring omission is Yankees three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge being left off their roster due to his ongoing recovery from a calf strain. The star slugger missed more than three months this season after suffering a fractured rib, and he injured his calf in his seventh game back in the lineup.

Judge had previously expressed optimism that he would be able to return in time for Tuesday's Game 1 against the Red Sox, despite Yankees manager Aaron Boone indicating that he would be sidelined.

"My goal is to come back as soon as I can," Judge told reporters last week. "That's what we're doing right now. If he says I'm not going to be ready, I've got no control over that. I got control over what I can do to try to get back as soon as I can. If you ask me if I'm gonna be back, I'm gonna tell you, I'm doing everything I can every single day I show up here to get back and be ready to go."

Now, the Yankees will officially have to forge ahead in their wild-card series against the Red Sox without their team captain on the field. New York has a talented pitching rotation led by AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler, but the hitters will have to step up if the team wants to avoid another early playoff exit.

articles.body: There are as many as 22 games remaining if a team goes to the World Series, and the distance in every series, to end the 2026 season. If you don't tune into playoff baseball, you're missing out. A lot of people, myself included, praise the NHL for having a great postseason, but baseball might be just as good. The Astros have the experience and a potential MVP in Yordan Alvarez. Their offense is almost certainly better than the White Sox. In terms of pitching matchups, I think it is fairly close. This will come down to whichever team is less likely to make a mistake. The Astros are 5-2 against the White Sox this year. I think the White Sox, even with their inexperience, are in a better spot to win the series. The Astros have shown they are an average team all year long. I like the White Sox to win, and I like this series to go 3 games. PHILLIES AVOID COLLAPSE, ASTROS SNEAK IN AS MLB POSTSEASON IS SET Yankees vs. Red Sox Another chapter in the storied histories of these two clubs. The Red Sox have been one of the hottest teams in baseball for the past few months. The Yankees have been consistent all season. Offensively, the series may hinge on how well Ben Rice will do. Aaron Judge is unlikely to play in the series, but New York has played well without him. The Red Sox seem to have a bit more of a balanced offense. I think the pitching edge comes on the Yankees side. They have the likely Cy Young winner going in Game 1, then they can send out Max Fried, and finally Gerrit Cole for their three starters. Braves vs. Phillies The Atlanta Braves host the Philadelphia Phillies, and this is a very similar series to the Yankees and Red Sox. I'd lean to them since they have home-field advantage and likely will take the opener. I really need to see how the Philadelphia rotation aligns before wagering on it. Padres vs. Cubs I'm taking the Padres, and I'm taking over 2.5 games in this one. Simply put, the Cubs don't have the pitching staff to advance. The offense has carried them, but as pitching gets tougher, it will be harder for them to score and be successful. Their defense could make a difference, but I just don't see it happening. articles.body:
Aaron Judge is reportedly not on the New York Yankees ' roster for their wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox , according to Jack Curry of the YES Network.

Judge's status for the wild-card round had been in question since the Yankees placed him on the injured list due to a calf strain on Sept. 18. On Sept. 22, manager Aaron Boone announced that the Yankees were planning to play without Judge in the wild-card round.

The injury list placement was Judge's second of the season after a stress fracture in one of his upper ribs sidelined him for three months. He struggled in his return, as he went 4-for-23 at the plate before the calf injury sidelined him a second time.

But Judge rebutted Boone's comments a day later, telling ESPN that he was preparing to play in the wild-card round.

"That's what the plan is," Judge said. "Try to get my body ready so I'm ready to go."

The call was ultimately left to the Yankees, and Judge made his final case to the team Monday afternoon in a batting practice session as the team prepared for their wild-card series.

The session was his first formal workout since he landed on the injured list, and it included multiple rounds of light batting practice before simulated at-bats against Yankees pitchers.

While Judge had taken swings since his calf injury, he told reporters that he'd been limited to running on an anti-gravity treadmill designed for rehabilitation . He'd yet to run the bases during his rehab process.

His session Monday left Yankees brass less than a day to make a decision on his status before Tuesday's 10 a.m. ET deadline for wild-card rosters to be submitted. The team ultimately decided Judge wasn't ready for action, leaving the outfielder to try to prepare for a return during a possible American League Division Series if the Yankees advance.

Also for this series, Giancarlo Stanton , who hasn't played since April due to multiple calf injuries, managed to make the Yankees' roster. Garrett Crochet , who has been sidelined since April due to a left shoulder issue, will also make his return for Boston.

articles.title: Cam Schlittler and Payton Tolle set up a potential pitching masterclass as MLB playoffs open at Yankee Stadium
articles.summary: Payton Tolle and likely American League Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler face off as the Red Sox and Yankees open their MLB postseason at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body: As a fan, I'm bummed that football is over until Thursday, but as a sports bettor, I'm happy to see it go after a brutal NFL week. Rather than focus on the bad, let's look toward the good things happening today. We have the MLB playoffs starting today, the NHL has its regular season beginning, and the WNBA has more playoff games. It will be a great day, and it starts early with the Phillies and Braves playing at 2 p.m. ET. However, I have my eyes set on the game between the Red Sox and Yankees, starting at 8 p.m. ET. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Boston Red Sox found a way to make it to the postseason after a disastrous start to the season. They were just 9-17 on Friday, April 24, and that was their fourth straight loss, all to AL East opponents. They ended up firing their manager, but things really didn't improve all that much. They were 29-43 around the middle of June. Then, almost like a light switch, they found a way to start winning. From June 25 until the end of the season, the team went 55-29. Over the course of a full 162-game season, that would give them almost 110 wins. It was one of the best runs in their history. Now they have the tough task of making it worthwhile against the Yankees. In order to try to get the first game of the series, they are sending out Payton Tolle. For the season, Tolle went 9-6 with a 3.03 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. He isn't one of the more well-known arms in the rotation, but he did turn in a solid performance. He was better on the road than he was at home with a 2.50 road ERA and a .202 opposing batting average. He was also spectacular against the Yankees this season, going 13.0 innings in two starts and allowing just four hits and one earned run while striking out 18 hitters. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Yankees didn't have any super hot streaks. Instead, they used a consistently successful approach this year, and even weathered the storm when there were injuries. The Yankees ended the year with a 93-68 record, and they were 12 games above average at home. This season saw the Yankees have success without Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton for a large portion of the year. They got great performances from guys like Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger instead. Rice led the team in homers and RBIs, turning in the best performance of his career. Speaking of guys who turned in the best performance of their career, Cam Schlittler is likely to be the American League Cy Young winner. Schlittler went 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and a 0.92 WHIP for the year. He was dominant in every facet of the pitching game. However, if you were going to get to Schlittler, it was probably at Yankee Stadium instead of on the road. He had 16 starts, one fewer than on the road, and had a 2.98 ERA at home, allowing 28 earned runs over 84.2 innings. For reference, he allowed 14 earned runs over 109 innings on the road. Schlittler was also great against the Red Sox this season, holding them to just two solo homers in 24.1 innings against him this season. That's good for a 0.74 ERA in four starts. With both of these pitchers, we can see how good they've been all season, but especially against their opponent. We will see what happens and if they can keep this going in the postseason. I personally believe we can and see this game going under 6.5 runs. I think this is likely to be a low-scoring game, but I don't have much confidence in either side. Give me the under 6.5.
